What the website includes

WHAT A CRE WEBSITE
needs.

Owners and landlords use the site to judge whether your firm can represent their property. Tenants, buyers, and cooperating brokers use it to find a space and the person to call.

01

Listings with property details

Size, price or rate, zoning, photos, a site plan where one exists, the brochure or OM, and the listing broker’s contact.

02

Broker profiles

Each broker’s property types, markets, notable assignments, and contact details.

03

04

An inquiry reaches the broker on that listing with the property already named.

05

Clear page titles, structured data, fast mobile loading, accessible markup, and redirects from an old site.

Keeping listings current

MANUAL, A FEED,
OR A platform.

How listings reach the website affects cost and upkeep more than any design decision, so we settle it first.

Manually maintained listings

Suited to a firm with a modest number of active assignments. Each listing is a full page that you or we update when the availability changes. This approach is included in a standard scope.

A listings feed

Firms that already maintain listings in a system such as Buildout, or through LoopNet’s LoopLink, can display that inventory on the website. We scope the integration and the listing pages before work begins.

A CRE website platform

Template platforms are quicker to set up and cost less at the start. They also look like many other brokerage sites and give you less control over pages and search. We will tell you plainly if a platform suits your firm better. Read our guide to CRE website templates.

Your project

WEBSITE
scope.

Your proposal confirms the pages, content, schedule, price, and any ongoing services.

  • Up to 6 core pages, 10 listing entries, and 10 team profiles
  • Your supplied company copy, property details, and photography
  • Mobile layout, inquiry forms, and two revision rounds

A standard scope uses your approved content and manually maintained listings. Hosting, domain registration, and ongoing updates are itemized in the quote. IDX, CRM integrations, portals, extensive migration, and new copy are scoped separately before work begins.

We reply within an hour during business hours, and we only use your details to answer you. No mailing lists.

Let’s talk

Questions

What does a commercial real estate website cost?

We quote each website after a short conversation. The cost depends on the number of pages and listings, whether we write the copy, and any listing feed or migration. What a commercial real estate website costs explains the ranges.

Do you only work with commercial real estate firms?

No. We work on websites and marketing for brokerages, property owners, property management companies, and other real estate businesses.

Can you also produce the listing materials?

Yes. We design property websites, offering memorandums, leasing brochures, and property branding, so the website and the materials can share one design.

How long will it take?

Most brokerage sites take a few weeks, depending on listings, writing, photography, and approvals. We confirm the schedule in the proposal.

Can you work with our existing photos and brand?

Yes. Send the photography, logo, brand guidelines, and any current website. New photography or brand work can be added if the project needs it.

Where is Endcap based?

Orange County, California. We work with brokerages across Southern California and further afield. See real estate web design in Orange County.
